summary: Bound checkpoint capture snapshots with selective below-cut mutation fencing, reduce replay memory, and keep proof rollback journals on disk.

replay.detail: Mission-run and planning replay retain ordered claim IDs and decode one body at a time instead of retaining every body. Existing bounded base-replay pages remain unchanged. Projection ordering, per-claim quarantine and proof comparisons are unchanged; no replay is forced on upgrade.

schema.detail: SQLite storage version 17 to 18 adds checkpoint_capture_epoch with a persistent mutation epoch, monotonic sealed-envelope frontier and accepted-time cut highwater. Guard trigger version 2 atomically drops/recreates earlier blanket predicates and advances the epoch so old captures restart. Earlier version-18 PR-head stores gain cut_unix_ms and trigger_version columns with default zero while preserving their epoch/frontier. Reopens preserve all bounds without repeating migration. No history scan, body rewrite or projection rebuild is required. The local storage registry/digest changes independently of the unchanged claim/wire digest. Proof copies retain disk-backed rollback journals and temporary storage with a fixed 2 MiB page-cache target.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules or digest change. Sealed envelope cuts and canonical ordering remain unchanged.

compatibility.detail: No replicated claim, checkpoint rule, wire protocol or response-shape change. Capture registers its cut and sealed frontier once, only when their retained highwaters increase; retries keep the original seal/cut and reread the epoch without another durable frontier update. Every bounded metadata, body, protection and tombstone snapshot checks that epoch. Below-cut captured content, canonical dependencies, protection references, repairs and tombstones restart capture; three invalidations fail closed. Normal above-cut replicated envelope admission/projection updates and identical ignored duplicate reoffers do not invalidate, even when the envelope is already inside the row frontier. Newer duplicates changing a captured claim's canonical MIN(position), OLD/NEW captured protection, late-claim exclusion witnesses and successful below-cut envelope REPLACE remain fenced. Accepted-time parsing is a prerequisite owned by #2106, not introduced again here. Stable older binaries reject storage version 18; earlier version-18 PR-head binaries using guard version 1 cannot safely use version-2 cut-aware storage or coexist with upgraded captures.

downtime.detail: Requires the normal process restart to initialize storage version 18 and guard trigger version 2. The migration adds missing guard columns and atomically replaces triggers without replaying history or rebuilding projections. Restart-to-API and restart-to-health duration have not been measured for this change.

manual.detail: The checkpoint scratch directory needs disk space for both the database copy and its rollback journal. Capture releases each bounded read snapshot before the next page, allowing the WAL to advance instead of pinning it for the entire body pass. Preserve a pre-upgrade database snapshot if binary rollback is needed. No setting, identity migration or store repair is required.

recovery.detail: The additive storage upgrade preserves existing claims and projections. Stable older binaries refuse version 18; earlier version-18 PR-head guard-v1 binaries cannot safely operate the cut-aware guard-v2 schema. Their copied stores migrate forward only. Restore a pre-upgrade database snapshot before binary rollback, or roll forward with the upgraded store. Do not reset the epoch/frontier/cut or manually downgrade user_version or trigger_version on a mutated store. Proof scratch files are removed on completion or error.
